title: Key Changes in GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C for FY 2019-20
excerpt: A practical overview of key GST annual return and reconciliation points for FY 2019-20.
author: VK&S Team

content.text: GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C require taxpayers to reconcile outward supplies, input tax credit, taxes paid and adjustments reported during the financial year. For FY 2019-20, the focus was on accurate reconciliation, proper disclosure of amendments and careful review of auto-populated data.

items: Match turnover reported in GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and financial statements.
Review input tax credit availed, reversed and reclaimed during the year.
Check amendments, credit notes, debit notes and year-end adjustments.
Verify tax paid through cash ledger and credit ledger before filing.

content.text: The annual return process should not be treated as a mechanical upload. It is a closing reconciliation exercise and should be reviewed with supporting ledgers, returns and management explanations before final submission.

title: Section 115BAA - New Corporate Tax Regime
excerpt: A concise note on the concessional corporate tax regime and practical evaluation points for companies.
author: VK&S Team

content.text: Section 115BAA introduced an option for eligible domestic companies to pay tax at a concessional rate subject to prescribed conditions. The option requires evaluation of available incentives, deductions, brought forward losses and long-term tax impact.

items: Identify deductions, incentives or exemptions that may not be available after opting.
Evaluate brought forward losses and depreciation linked to restricted deductions.
Compare tax outflow under the existing regime and concessional regime.
Document management approval and basis of selection for future reference.

content.text: The regime can be useful, but the decision should be made after a computation-based comparison rather than only by looking at the headline tax rate.

title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code - One Year of Resolution
excerpt: Practical observations from early IBC proceedings and learnings for creditors, debtors and stakeholders.
author: VK&S Team

content.text: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code changed the approach to stressed assets by introducing a time-bound resolution framework. Early proceedings highlighted the importance of documentation, creditor coordination and realistic resolution planning.

items: Maintain clear loan, security, invoice and default records before initiating or defending proceedings.
Review claims carefully and support them with complete documentation.
Assess resolution plans with commercial viability and statutory requirements in mind.
Track timelines closely because delay can materially affect recovery and resolution outcomes.

content.text: IBC-related work requires coordinated financial, legal and operational review. Each matter should be assessed on its facts, applicable law and professional role permitted for the firm.
